what_it_does: This paper presents a high-power wireless charging system that can deliver 50 watts (about as much power as a laptop charger) to a device's battery using inductive wireless coupling—the same principle that powers many modern phone chargers. The core challenge is that the transmitter and receiver need to communicate constantly to adjust power safely and handle signal reflections, and traditional communication methods produce annoying acoustic noise in the receiver coil (the vibrating wire loop that picks up power). The design achieves 98% efficiency (only 2% wasted as heat) by using a hybrid receiver that can decode messages using either voltage or current sensing, switching between them based on what works best at each moment.
